label: Point Tupper site brief: key places
notice: Key places for the Point Tupper data-centre campus, each from a public source. The campus footprint has not been published, so it is not drawn.

properties.label: EverWind terminal
properties.name: Point Tupper Terminal jetty (EverWind)
properties.note: EverWind's Point Tupper Terminal: a 7.7-million-barrel storage terminal with 39 aboveground tanks and two deep-water berths. EverWind announced the data-centre campus for Point Tupper on October 16, 2026.
properties.located_by: The meteorological station on the EverWind jetty, at 45°34′25.140″ N, 61°20′36.708″ W, as the registration gives it.
properties.source: EverWind Point Tupper Green Hydrogen/Ammonia Project, Environmental Assessment registration (December 2022), sections 3.3 and 6 (Table 6.3)

properties.label: Generating station
properties.name: Point Tupper Generating Station (Nova Scotia Power)
properties.note: Nova Scotia Power's generating station at Point Tupper. Turn on Electrical transmission lines and Electrical substations to see the mapped grid around it.
properties.source: Wikidata Q7208178; Nova Scotia Power, About our facilities

properties.label: Landrie Lake
properties.name: Landrie Lake (industrial water supply)
properties.note: Built by the Province in 1969 to supply raw water to Point Tupper industry; now run by the Landrie Lake Water Utility. EverWind says the campus's closed-loop cooling will draw about 100,000 litres a day in phase 1 and about 500,000 litres a day after expansion, about 1% of the lake's stated safe yield of 34 million litres a day (company figures, as reported by The Canadian Press on October 16, 2026).
properties.located_by: Wikidata item Q22360244 (public-domain coordinates). Turn on Water features for the lake outline.
properties.source: Landrie Lake Water Utility, Little River Pumping and Transmission System EA registration (January 2026); The Canadian Press, October 16, 2026
